E000.what: Two things have the same name (or a name is reserved).
E000.fix: Rename one of them: select it and change its name in the Inspector.

E001.what: A block is missing something it needs plugged in, usually an AI model.
E001.fix: Click the coloured square on the block's left (the input named in the message) and pick what to plug in, e.g. an AI model.

E002.what: An arrow points at an input or output that does not exist (any more).
E002.fix: Click the arrow, press Delete, and draw it again from the right dot.

E003.what: Something refers to a block that was deleted.
E003.fix: Delete the dangling arrow, or pick another block in the setting the message names.

E004.what: A setting of this block is missing or not valid.
E004.fix: Select the block and fill in the setting marked in red in the Inspector.

E005.what: This block type is not known on this server (or was put in the wrong place).
E005.fix: Delete the block and add it again from the palette.

E006.what: An arrow connects two things that cannot be connected that way.
E006.fix: Steps connect with grey arrows (right dot → left dot). Add-ons such as AI models plug into a step's coloured inputs. Delete the arrow and redraw it.

E007.what: A resource has a name Python reserves (like class, import or builder), so the exported code could not use it.
E007.fix: Rename the resource in the Inspector, for example add a word: fast_model instead of builder.

E010.what: There is no path from Start to Finish, so a run could never finish.
E010.fix: Connect Start to your first step, and your last step to Finish. Tip: click a step's right-hand dot to pick what comes next.

E011.what: This step can never run: nothing leads to it from Start.
E011.fix: Connect an earlier step (or Start) to it, or delete it if you don't need it.

E012.what: A path of this “Choose a path” block goes nowhere (or goes to two places).
E012.fix: Connect each path (the dots on its right) to exactly one step, or to Finish.

E013.what: A condition (rule) is not written correctly.
E013.fix: Check the rule in the Inspector. Example of a valid rule: state.priority == "high".

E014.what: The text template has a typo, usually unbalanced {{ }} brackets.
E014.fix: Every {{ needs a matching }}. Example: Hello {{ state.name }}.

E015.what: This step is a dead end: nothing comes after it.
E015.fix: Click its right-hand dot and choose the next step, or Finish.

E016.what: “Wait for all” is waiting for a branch that may never arrive, so the run would hang.
E016.fix: Only connect branches into it that always run (not ones after a “Choose a path”).

E017.what: This AI model needs the server address of its provider.
E017.fix: Select the AI model block and fill in Base URL (for local models, e.g. http://localhost:11434 for Ollama).

E018.what: Something inside this group of steps is broken.
E018.fix: Double-click the group to look inside; the message says what is wrong there.

E019.what: The group of steps uses a block with the same name as one outside, but set up differently.

E020.what: Two steps run at the same time and both overwrite the same data field, so one answer would be lost.
E020.fix: Make them write different fields, or set the field to “append” (keep a list) in the data fields list.

E021.what: A step uses a data field that does not exist yet.
E021.fix: Click empty canvas, then add the field (“+ Channel”) with the exact name from the message, or pick an existing field in the step's settings.

E022.what: “Repeat for each item” runs copies at the same time, and they overwrite the same field.
E022.fix: Set that field to “append” (keep a list) so every copy's result is kept.

E023.what: A step reads a data field that does not exist.
E023.fix: Add the field (click empty canvas, “+ Channel”) or correct its name in the step.

E024.what: This AI model runs in your own cloud account (AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI) and needs a region: the place its prompts are sent to and processed in. It always uses the provider's own address.
E024.fix: Select the AI model block and fill in Region (e.g. eu-central-1 on AWS, europe-west4, eu or global on Google Cloud), or ask whoever runs the server to set a default region. Clear Base URL.

E030.what: The chosen AI model cannot do what this step asks (use tools or give structured answers).
E030.fix: Pick a more capable model in the AI model block, or remove the tools / structured output.

E031.what: The same tool is plugged in twice.
E031.fix: Delete one of the two arrows.

E032.what: A helper agent is set up incompletely (it needs a description) or is plugged in twice.
E032.fix: Select the helper agent and fill in “When to use it”, or delete the duplicate arrow.

E033.what: The approval list names a tool that is not plugged into this agent.
E033.fix: Plug the tool in, or remove it from “Tools that need approval”.

E034.what: A file permission path is not allowed.
E034.fix: Use a full path starting with / and without .. or ~.

E035.what: The same add-on is plugged in twice (or the Planning Agent already has it built in).

E036.what: Two file storages are set up for the same place.
E036.fix: Remove one, or give them different folders.

E037.what: A step lets whoever calls the published workflow answer, and also keeps the person who started the run from deciding. The caller is the one who started it, so the two contradict each other.
E037.fix: Untick one of the two under “Who may decide”.

E041.what: This block runs code on the server, which is only allowed when you run AgentCanvas yourself.
E041.fix: Use it in a local install, or replace it with a Web API tool.

E042.what: This app connector starts a program on the server, which an admin must allow first.
E042.fix: Ask an admin to enable local MCP, or use a connector with a URL.

E043.what: A tool or remote agent is allowed to reach private or internal network addresses, which the hosted service never allows.
E043.fix: Turn off "Allow private network" on it, and give it a public address instead.

E045.what: Publishing pins an app connector’s tools as you reviewed them, so a server that changes later cannot reach the published agent. This connector’s tools were never listed, so there is nothing to pin.
E045.fix: Select the connector, click Browse tools and check its tools (untick the ones the agent should not have), then publish.

E050.what: A password or API key is typed straight into a setting, where others could see it.
E050.fix: Store it as a project secret (Workspace → Secrets) and pick it from the list instead.

E051.what: A secret is referenced by a name that is not a plain variable name, so exports could not pass it as a setting.
E051.fix: Use a secret whose name has only letters, digits and _ (for example OPENAI_API_KEY).

E070.what: This block both pauses for a person and changes something outside, which would happen twice when the run resumes.
E070.fix: Move the outside change into a separate step after the approval.

E071.what: This memory is kept per user, but the workflow does not know who the user is.
E071.fix: In the workflow settings (click empty canvas), add a context field such as user_id with source “user”, or share the memory per workflow instead.

E080.what: The Python function is not in your Workspace.
E080.fix: Pick a function from the Workspace (scripts., tools. or nodes.).

E095.what: Your organisation's rules do not allow this.
E095.fix: Read the rule in the message and change the workflow to follow it, or ask an admin.

E096.what: An organisation rule could not be checked.
E096.fix: Ask an admin to look at the rule; the message says which one.

E097.what: A Wait block is missing how long or until when to wait, or a duration, time, time zone or event it cannot use.
E097.fix: Select the Wait block and fill in how long (e.g. 3d or 2h 30m), the time (e.g. 2026-12-01T09:00), or the event and its time limit. A wait lasts at most a year.

E999.what: One of the checks failed while checking this workflow (a problem in AgentCanvas, not in your workflow). The other checks still ran.
E999.fix: Report it with the message shown. You can keep editing; publishing stays blocked until the check runs.

I010.what: This block uses a feature that may still change upstream.
I010.fix: Nothing to do; just be aware it may change in a future version.

I011.what: This step names who may decide it. AgentCanvas checks that before the run continues; code exported from the workflow does not.
I011.fix: Nothing to do for runs on AgentCanvas. If you run the export elsewhere, check who answers its pauses in your own code.

P001.what: The workflow's framework cannot run this block (or the framework is not installed on this server).
P001.fix: Pick another framework in the workflow settings (click empty canvas → Framework), or replace the block with one the framework can run. The badges at the top show what each framework is missing.

P002.what: This framework can run the block only by imitating it, so it may behave a little differently.
P002.fix: Nothing to do if that is fine; the message says what differs. Pick a framework that runs it natively to avoid it.

P003.what: This workflow could move to some installed frameworks but not to others.
P003.fix: Nothing to do. To make it portable, replace the blocks the message names.

P004.what: This block is designed for a different framework than the rest of the workflow.
P004.fix: Nothing to do for now: it runs on the workflow's framework. Choose “Same as the workflow” in the block's settings to clear it.

P005.what: This Agent block is designed for another framework, and that framework cannot take part of it (add-ons, a kind of tool, or the structured output).
P005.fix: Remove what the message names, or choose “Same as the workflow” under Designed for so LangGraph runs the agent.

P006.what: This Agent block is designed for a framework that is not installed on this server, so its runs stop with an error.
P006.fix: Ask an admin to install the package the message names on the server, or export the agent and run it where the framework is installed.

P007.what: This framework does not apply a block's retry, timeout, cache or error route (its node policies): the block runs once, with no time limit, and an error ends the run.
P007.fix: Remove the policy from the block (or the workflow's defaults), handle the failure inside the flow (a path after the step), or switch the workflow to LangGraph, which applies node policies.

W001.what: These steps form a loop with no way out, so it would only stop at the safety limit.
W001.fix: Add a “Choose a path” step in the loop with a path that leaves it.

W002.what: An agent can use a tool that changes or deletes things, without asking a person first.
W002.fix: Select the agent and add the tool to “Tools that need approval”.

W003.what: A private data field is filled but never used.
W003.fix: Use it in a later step, or delete it.

W010.what: This AI model name is not in the built-in list, so its abilities cannot be checked.
W010.fix: Double-check the spelling (provider:model, e.g. openai:gpt-5.5) or pick one from the list.

W011.what: Support for this AI provider is not installed on the server.
W011.fix: Ask whoever runs the server to install the package named in the message, or pick another provider.

W012.what: An arrow leaves a path that the “Choose a path” block does not have any more.
W012.fix: Delete that arrow, or add a rule with that path name.

W013.what: “Wait for all” has fewer than two branches coming in, so it has nothing to wait for.
W013.fix: Connect at least two branches into it, or delete it.

W015.what: The cost limit cannot count this model, because its price is unknown.
W015.fix: Use a token limit instead, or a model with a known price.

W024.what: A model in “Use the cheapest of” is listed twice, is a local model (a run never picks those by price), or has no known price (it is chosen only when no priced model qualifies).
W024.fix: Remove the repeat, move a local model to the backup models, or ask your operator to set the price.

W016.what: This backup model is already tried before it, so it adds nothing when the model fails.
W016.fix: Pick a backup model from another provider.

W017.what: “Retry AI calls” comes after “Backup models” and is set to carry on when its retries run out, so it answers the failure itself and the backup models are never tried.
W017.fix: Select the retry add-on and set “When retries are exhausted” to error, or connect it before the backup models.

W018.what: Something inside this group of steps needs attention.
W018.fix: Double-click the group to look inside.

W019.what: A safety check is set to only flag problems, but its verdict is not saved anywhere, so no later step can act on it.
W019.fix: Select the safety block and pick a field in “Save yes/no in”, then branch on it with a “Choose a path” step (e.g. state.flagged == true). Or set “When it fails” to stop.

W020.what: This model does not take a temperature (or top_p, top_k), so the setting is left out.
W020.fix: Clear the setting. To make answers more varied or more exact, say so in the prompt.

P008.what: This workflow has file or image fields, but the framework it is set to run on does not show them to an AI model. The file is carried along as plain data and no step reads it.
P008.fix: Run the workflow on LangChain (Framework in the workflow settings), where Ask AI and AI Agent steps show the files to their model.

W025.what: This step is shown a file or image field, but its model cannot see images. Images are left out and a PDF is read as plain text, so layout, tables and scans are lost.
W025.fix: Pick a model that takes images, or limit the step to the fields it needs under “Files to show the AI”.

W026.what: The workflow’s budget stops runs on AgentCanvas, but an export of this workflow does not enforce some of its limits: the exported code runs past them.
W026.fix: Keep the limit for runs on AgentCanvas. Before running the export elsewhere, set a spending cap at the model provider, or check the limits the message names in your own code (GAPS.md lists them).

W027.what: This agent names who may approve its tool calls, but none of its tools needs approval, so it never asks anyone.
W027.fix: Add the tools that need a person’s approval, or clear “Who may approve its tool calls”.

W021.what: A header or environment value that looks like a key is typed in as plain text. Runs work, but an export would write it into the code, so exports refuse it.
W021.fix: Store it as a project secret (Workspace → Secrets) and pick it from the list instead.

W023.what: The provider stops serving this model on the day shown; after it, every call to it fails.
W023.fix: Pick a newer model from the list before that day (the provider names a successor).

W028.what: This AI model runs in your own cloud account, but no credentials for it were found: neither project secrets nor an identity of the server's.
W028.fix: Add the project secrets the message names (Workspace → Secrets), or ask whoever runs the server to give it a cloud identity (an IAM role on AWS, Workload Identity on Google Cloud).

W029.what: A region or Google Cloud project is set on a model that is not in your own cloud account, so it is not used.
W029.fix: Clear the setting, or pick an AWS Bedrock or Google Vertex AI model if the region matters.

W045.what: An app connector’s server added or changed tools since this workflow was published. The deployment leaves those tools out (or stops), because nobody reviewed them.
W045.fix: Select the connector, click Browse tools and review what changed. If you trust it, publish again: the new version pins the tools as they are now.

W095.what: This goes against a recommended organisation rule.
W095.fix: Read the rule in the message; consider changing the workflow.

W096.what: A Wait block waits for an event without a key: one such event ends every run that waits for it.
W096.fix: Set “Only the event with this key” (e.g. {{ state.order_id }}) and send the same value as "key" in the event's data.

run_errors.what: A safety block found a problem (personal data, prompt injection, harmful content or a wrong output format) and was set to stop the run.
run_errors.fix: The message says which block and why. If the text is fine, adjust the block's settings (e.g. the sensitivity threshold); to carry on instead, set “When it fails” to flag and branch on the saved verdict with “Choose a path”.

run_errors.what: The AI provider refused the API key (missing or wrong).
run_errors.fix: Open Model (home page) or the AI model block and check the key. Keys are stored as project secrets named after the provider, e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.

run_errors.what: The AI provider says you are sending too many requests, or your credit has run out.
run_errors.fix: Wait a minute and run again, or check your plan and billing with the provider.

run_errors.pattern: connection refused|ECONNREFUSED|failed to establish|connect(ion)? error|name or service not known|getaddrinfo
run_errors.what: Could not reach the AI model's server.
run_errors.fix: If you use a local model (Ollama, LM Studio…), make sure it is running and the Base URL is right. Otherwise check your internet connection.

run_errors.what: The AI provider does not know this model name.
run_errors.fix: Check the model name in the AI model block (e.g. anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5), or pick one from the list.

run_errors.what: A step took too long and was stopped.
run_errors.fix: Run again; if it keeps happening, raise Timeout on the AI model block or simplify the prompt.

run_errors.what: The workflow went round a loop too many times.
run_errors.fix: Add a “Choose a path” step with a way out of the loop, or a limit add-on on the agent.

run_errors.what: A step used a data field that had no value yet.
run_errors.fix: Check the {{ state.<field> }} names in your prompts match your data fields, and that the run input fills them, e.g. {"question": "…"}.

run_errors.what: Some input was not in the expected format.
run_errors.fix: Run input must be JSON, e.g. {"question": "What is AI?"}: curly braces, field names in double quotes.

run_errors.what: The workflow still has problems, so it cannot run.
run_errors.fix: Open Problems at the bottom; each one says how to fix it.

run_errors.what: You (or the workflow) are not allowed to do this.
run_errors.fix: Ask a project admin for the builder role, or for access to the resource named in the message.
